problem: First chat entry could leave part of the final image message below the viewport after later self-sizing or composer/safe-area layout.
findings: Chat disabled the renderer initial-replace bottom layout fallback.
Initial explicit last-item scroll was a one-shot command; geometry updates only changed the append-follow flag and did not correct a remaining bottom gap.
changes: Enable the renderer initial-load bottom fallback when opening at the latest end, while focused/history entry starts with that fallback disabled.
Keep initial latest-end anchoring through measured content/viewport/inset changes; correct to the actual content edge if more than one point remains.
Suppress repeated corrections for unchanged geometry. Real user scroll input, focused-message navigation and history browsing release the initial pin.
Leave the existing stable-ID own-send/history transaction logic and the external MessagingUI checkout unchanged.

cases: Actual conversation view with nine image rows: entire last row settles inside the unobscured collection viewport.
Same hosted view after adding an 80pt bottom safe-area inset: last row remains fully visible.
Image content height growth and composer viewport changes correct remaining gaps.
Repeated unchanged geometry does not loop; empty/zero-sized layout is ignored.
User scroll and focused/history entry prevent forced tail restoration.
Existing timeline identity and acknowledgement transactions remain stable.

visualInspection: Incoming at latest: message 17 and its timestamp fully above composer.
After user scroll and incoming append: history messages 7–11 remain visible, not forced to newest 29.
Three consecutive sends: last outgoing message and timestamp remain fully above composer.

limitations: Hosted simulator geometry validation is not a physical-device reproduction of the user screenshot.
Hosted image rows use synthetic media references and layout placeholders; actual phone-photo decoding was not reproduced in that test.
